patch.value: The measurement ratchet has a single polarity: a filed number can only be enforced as a ceiling, so no quality floor this project wants to hold is expressible

The tracker measurement ratchet in scripts/release/tracker-measurement-gate.mjs turns a number an item filed about itself into an enforced limit. It has exactly one polarity. A declaration carries a `ceiling`, the evaluator computes `exceeded = observed > ceiling`, the re-baseline path takes `Math.min(declaration.ceiling, entry.observed)` so a declaration can only ever be lowered, and the failure text states the rule directly: a filed measurement is a ceiling. There is no floor concept in the document schema, the evaluator, the re-baseline path, or the negative control.

The consequence is that the mechanism can express "this defect population may not grow" and cannot express "this quality property may not fall". Every property this project wants to hold or raise is therefore inexpressible as an enforced declaration. The graph carries 11,291 deduplicated directed edges across 2,365 nodes; nothing prevents a change from removing ten thousand of them. Typed reachability to an outcome is the property the strategic layer exists to provide; nothing prevents it from regressing. The same asymmetry covers coverage of a lineage, recovery-closure scoring, context precision, and every future metric whose good direction is up.

The asymmetry is not a gap in coverage, it is a gap in the vocabulary, so no amount of new declarations can close it. Twenty-five declarations exist today and all twenty-five are ceilings, because a ceiling is the only thing a declaration can be.

The risk this leaves open is concrete and already reachable through a supported flag: `--dep-remove` deletes every row matching its selector, and a well-formed unmatchable selector exits zero. A mutation that silently strips typed relationships from the record reduces every graph population, so every existing declaration passes more comfortably than before. The ratchet reads a mass deletion of the project's most carefully authored structure as an improvement.

A declaration may express a floor as well as a ceiling, and the evaluator reports a violation when an observed value falls below a declared floor; The re-baseline path raises a floor toward the observed value and never lowers one, mirroring the existing ceiling behaviour in the opposite direction; A negative control proves a floor violation fails the gate, alongside the existing control that proves a ceiling violation fails it; The total deduplicated directed edge count and the count of active items resolving to an outcome are declared as floors, so a change that strips typed relationships fails before merge; The failure text names the polarity that was violated, so a reader can tell a shrinking quality property from a growing defect population

value.text:
Partially delivered 2026-08-07 by child pm-z0cfor, which is closed with linked script, declaration and spec artifacts. AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC5 are satisfied: a declaration may carry a floor, the evaluator reports floor_undercut, the re-baseline path raises floors and never lowers them, the negative control proves both directions fail, and the violation line names its polarity.

AC4 is half satisfied and the remaining half is genuinely blocked rather than deferred. graph-profile-edges-floor is declared at 11,318 and graph-profile-nodes-floor at 2,368, both baselined from the gate's own commit view, so a change that strips typed relationships now fails before merge. The second clause of AC4 — the count of active items resolving to an outcome, declared as a floor — cannot be written yet, because the only graph surface this gate can read is the audit profile and that object exposes no reachability field. pm-4vz6mz owns exposing it. This item stays open on that clause alone.

Worth recording for whoever picks it up: the polarity fix makes the enforcement layer able to protect a magnitude in both directions, and a magnitude is still all it can protect. Typed reachability, dominance and articulation are properties of paths, trees and connectivity, and none of them is an integer compared against another integer. That is the general form, recorded as horizon AF on pm-doxj, and it is upstream of this item rather than inside it.
